question.text: What is the difference between a foreign exchange swap and a currency swap?

answer.text: FX swap involves principal amount only, while a currency swap involves exchange of interest payments and/or principal amounts in different currencies
FX swap is exchange-traded while currency swap is OTC
FX swap involves only INR while currency swap involves only USD
There is no difference — they are the same product

explanation.text: The Logic: Page 40 of the NISM Series I Currency Derivatives workbook (December 2025) states that a foreign exchange swap exchanges the principal amount only on the short leg and reverses it later, whereas a currency swap commits the counterparties to exchange streams of interest payments and/or principal amounts in different currencies. It also notes that initial exchange of principal is not obligatory in a currency swap. The Trap: Saying a currency swap must involve both interest and principal is too narrow because principal exchange is not obligatory. The other distractors mis-describe the trading venue and currency scope. Note: Answer wording corrected from "both interest payments and principal" to "interest payments and/or principal amounts" to match page 40.
